record_identity.title: Deepfake investment campaign reportedly defrauded thousands of Swedish investors

incident_identity.historical_event_name: Deepfake investment campaign reportedly defrauded thousands of Swedish investors
incident_identity.date_basis: TV4 published its investigation on 24 October 2025; the fraud campaign was already operating before publication.

summary: Swedish reporting described dozens of AI-generated investment advertisements impersonating roughly 15–20 Swedish financial figures. TV4 attributed at least 5,000 victims and about SEK 500 million in aggregate losses to the campaign; those figures remain reported estimates rather than regulator-audited totals.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: TV4 reported that fraudsters used AI-generated video and fabricated endorsements from 15–20 Swedish financial figures across dozens of advertisements. It attributed the estimate of at least 5,000 victims and roughly SEK 500 million in losses to its investigation. Sveriges Radio separately reported the same scale and described the use of Gabriel Mellqvist's identity.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The campaign converted recognisable identities into apparent investment authority and used that false authority to induce financial decisions. The evidence supports both material financial loss and bounded reputational injury to the impersonated people.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: The occurrence shows how synthetic identity can transfer perceived professional authority into a fraudulent commercial purpose at population scale.
assessment_boundaries: The SEK 500 million figure is a reported aggregate estimate rather than a regulator-audited loss total.
The sources establish a campaign and victim scale but do not identify every advertisement, victim or transaction.

They do not establish that an AI system selected or pursued its own objective through an agency-impairing tactic; the AI-mediated false endorsement is already captured under the economic-solicitation and social-engineering classes.

external_requirement_assessments.applicability_basis: The reported campaign used AI-generated impersonations of Swedish financial figures in advertisements directed at Swedish investors in October 2025, after Article 5 began applying on 2 February 2025. The AI output was used in Sweden, bringing this occurrence within Article 2(1)(c) even though the generating provider and deployer are not identified. This is an occurrence-level scope decision, not attribution of legal responsibility.
external_requirement_assessments.finding_basis: TV4 and Sveriges Radio report dozens of AI-generated advertisements falsely depicting 15–20 Swedish financial figures as endorsing investments, directed at Swedish investors; they attribute at least 5,000 victims and approximately SEK 500 million in aggregate loss to the campaign. The fabricated endorsements materially misrepresented financial authority to influence investment choices, and the reported scale of realized loss supports significant harm. The totals remain attributed estimates, and this finding does not identify or assign liability to a provider or deployer.

external_requirement_assessments.applicability_basis: The campaign's AI-generated investment advertisements targeted Swedish investors in October 2025, after Article 5 began applying on 2 February 2025. The output was used in Sweden, satisfying the territorial connection in Article 2(1)(c); the provider and deployer remain unidentified, so this assessment does not assign responsibility.
external_requirement_assessments.finding_basis: The campaign materially engaged financial decision-making and caused substantial reported losses in Sweden, but the record does not establish that the scammers or AI practice selected or exploited people because of age, disability, or a specific social or economic situation. Financial loss by retail investors alone does not prove the statutory vulnerability element. That concrete condition remains unresolved, so the occurrence is ambiguous under Article 5(1)(b).
